title: At the market
summary: Shop for presents in Khan el-Khalili: say what things are made of, ask for a discount and bargain politely.
intro: Khan el-Khalili is Cairo's great old market, full of lanterns, silver, perfume and spices. Today you put هُنَاكَ and the plurals of things together: هُنَاكَ فَوَانِيس كَثِيرَة (there are many lanterns), هٰذِهِ الْفَوَانِيس قَدِيمَة (these lanterns are old). You also meet two verbs every market needs: يَشْتَرِي (to buy) and يَبِيعُ (to sell).
objectives: Name six things you can buy in a market
Say what something is made of with مِنَ: مِنَ الْفِضَّة
Ask for a discount politely and agree on a price
Use يَشْتَرِي (to buy) and يَبِيعُ (to sell)

realLife.title: Presents from Khan el-Khalili
realLife.story: Daniel wants to send presents to his parents in Chicago. On Saturday Layla and Sami take him to Khan el-Khalili. The narrow lanes are full of shops, the sellers call out to every visitor, and Daniel has to bargain in Arabic for the very first time.

sentences.en: There are many lanterns in the market.
sentences.literal: there (are) lanterns many (f) in the market

mistakes.why: Lanterns are things, so their plural takes a feminine singular adjective: kathīra.

sentences.en: The seller sells perfumes and silver.
sentences.literal: sells the seller the perfumes and the silver

sentences.en: This present is for my mother.
sentences.literal: this the present (is) for my mother

sentences.en: This necklace is made of silver.
sentences.literal: this the necklace (is) from the silver

mistakes.why: ʿiqd (necklace) is masculine, so it takes hādhā, even though the silver is feminine.

sentences.en: These lanterns are old and beautiful.
sentences.literal: these (f) the lanterns (are) old (f) and beautiful (f)

sentences.en: Is there a discount for students?
sentences.literal: (question) there (is) a discount for the students

dialogue.title: Bargaining in Khan el-Khalili
dialogue.culture: Bargaining is normal in markets like Khan el-Khalili, but always smile and stay friendly: it is a conversation, not a fight. A good rule is to start at about half the first price and meet in the middle. When the call to prayer (الْأَذَان) sounds from the nearby mosque of al-Hussein, some sellers close for a few minutes.

lines.ar: أَهْلًا بِكُمْ فِي خَانِ الْخَلِيلِيّ! عُمْرُ هٰذَا السُّوق أَكْثَرُ مِنْ سِتِّمِئَة سَنَة.
lines.en: Welcome to Khan el-Khalili! This market is more than six hundred years old.
segs: Khan (part of the market's name; lit. inn)

lines.ar: مَا أَجْمَلَ هٰذِهِ الشَّوَارِع الضَّيِّقَة! وَهُنَاكَ مَحَلَّات فِي كُلِّ مَكَان.
lines.en: How beautiful these narrow streets are! And there are shops everywhere you look.

lines.ar: أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَشْتَرِيَ هَدَايَا لِأَبِي وَأُمِّي فِي شِيكَاغُو. مَاذَا تَقْتَرِحُونَ؟
lines.en: I want to buy presents for my father and mother in Chicago. What do you suggest?

lines.ar: الْفَوَانِيس هُنَا جَمِيلَة جِدًّا، وَهُنَاكَ أَيْضًا عُطُور وَفِضَّة.
lines.en: The lanterns here are very beautiful, and there are also perfumes and silver.

lines.ar: تَفَضَّلُوا، تَفَضَّلُوا! عِنْدِي أَجْمَلُ الْفَوَانِيس فِي السُّوق، وَكُلُّهَا مِنَ النُّحَاس.
lines.en: Come in, come in! I have the most beautiful lanterns in the market, and they are all made of brass.

lines.ar: هٰذَا الْفَانُوس الصَّغِير جَمِيل. هَلْ هُوَ قَدِيم أَمْ جَدِيد؟
lines.en: This little lantern is beautiful. Is it old or new?

lines.ar: هُوَ جَدِيد، لٰكِنْ نَصْنَعُهُ بِالْيَد مِثْلَ الْفَوَانِيس الْقَدِيمَة. هُوَ بِخَمْسِمِئَة جُنَيْه.
lines.en: It is new, but we make it by hand, just like the old lanterns. It costs five hundred pounds.

lines.ar: يَا دَانْيَال، هٰذَا سِعْر لِلسُّيَّاح. اُطْلُبْ خَصْمًا، فَالْبَاعَة هُنَا يُحِبُّونَ الْمُسَاوَمَة.
lines.en: Daniel, that is a price for tourists. Ask for a discount: the sellers here love bargaining.

lines.ar: خَمْسُمِئَة كَثِير! أَنَا طَالِب فِي الْقَاهِرَة. هَلْ هُنَاكَ خَصْم لِلطُّلَّاب؟
lines.en: Five hundred is a lot! I am a student in Cairo. Is there a discount for students?

lines.ar: أَنْتَ تَتَكَلَّمُ الْعَرَبِيَّة؟ مَا شَاءَ اللّٰه! لَكَ خَصْم خَاصّ: أَرْبَعُمِئَة.
lines.en: You speak Arabic? How wonderful! You get a special discount: four hundred.

lines.ar: ثَلَاثُمِئَة، وَأَنَا أَشْتَرِي أَيْضًا زُجَاجَةَ عِطْر لِأُمِّي. مَا رَأْيُكَ؟
lines.en: Three hundred, and I will also buy a bottle of perfume for my mother. What do you think?

lines.ar: طَيِّب، ثَلَاثُمِئَة لِلْفَانُوس. وَعِطْرُ الْيَاسَمِين بِمِئَتَيْ جُنَيْه، وَهُوَ عِطْر مِصْرِيّ مُمْتَاز!
lines.en: All right, three hundred for the lantern. And the jasmine perfume is two hundred pounds; it is an excellent Egyptian perfume!

lines.ar: وَأَنَا أُرِيدُ هٰذَا الْعِقْد مِنَ الْفِضَّة. هَلْ تَبِيعُهُ لِي بِخَصْم أَيْضًا؟
lines.en: And I would like this silver necklace. Will you sell it to me with a discount too?

lines.ar: لَكِ وَلِصَدِيقِكِ؟ طَبْعًا! الْيَوْم كُلُّ الْأَسْعَار خَاصَّة لِلطُّلَّاب.
lines.en: For you and your friend? Of course! Today all the prices are special for students.
segs: and for your friend (to a woman)

lines.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا! أُحِبُّ هٰذَا السُّوق، وَأُحِبُّ الْمُسَاوَمَة بِالْعَرَبِيَّة أَيْضًا!
lines.en: Thank you very much! I love this market, and I love bargaining in Arabic too!

reading.title: A postcard to Chicago
reading.ar: مَرْحَبًا يَا أُمِّي! الْيَوْم كُنْتُ فِي سُوقِ خَانِ الْخَلِيلِيّ. هُنَاكَ مَحَلَّات كَثِيرَة، وَالشَّوَارِع ضَيِّقَة وَمُزْدَحِمَة. اِشْتَرَيْتُ لَكِ عِطْرًا مِصْرِيًّا، وَاشْتَرَيْتُ لِأَبِي فَانُوسًا جَمِيلًا. الْبَاعَة لُطَفَاء جِدًّا!
reading.en: Hello, Mum! Today I was at the Khan el-Khalili market. There are lots of shops, and the streets are narrow and crowded. I bought you an Egyptian perfume, and I bought Dad a beautiful lantern. The sellers are very kind!
segs: Khan (part of the market's name; lit. inn)

quiz.prompt: Fill the gap: 'There are many lanterns.'
What are the seller's lanterns made of?
What price do Daniel and the seller agree on for the lantern?
Which present does Daniel buy for his mother?
Which word begins with the throat sound ʿayn?

completion: Fantastic! You can shop in an Arab market, bargain politely and talk about plural things. Take the week test (80% to pass) to open Week 5.
